Mr. Mukesh Kalia, Counsel for the petitioner appears and presents the basic factual background.
2.  The petitioner and Samita Rani (now deceased) were married on 06th April, 2010, subsequently separated on 30th June, 2010.
Proceedings for divorce by way of mutual consent were pending.
Thereafter, Samita Rani committed suicide on 22nd April, 2012.
On 22nd June, 2012, anticipatory bail was granted to the petitioner.

FIR No.127/2017 was registered on 22nd April, 2012 under Sections 306/498A IPC.
3.
Subsequently, on 12th February, 2018, charge was framed against the petitioner under Section 306 IPC and he was discharged under Section 498A IPC.
The trial commenced and post recording the evidence an application was moved by the State for framing of charges under Section 3(2)(v) of the This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 17/07/2024 at 01:11:39 SC/ST Act.
The amended charge was framed on 18thOctober, 2019 which is impugned herein.

An objection was taken that under Rule 7(1) of 1995 under the SC/ST Act which mandates that offences under the Act can only be investigated by an officer not below the rank of a Deputy Superintendent of Police.

The petitioner, therefore, raised an issue that the additional charge will not survive considering the investigation had been carried out by the competent officer under the IPC which is below the Deputy Superintendent of Police.

4. This contention was rejected by the impugned order on the basis that Section 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST Act encompasses offences under the IPC whereas Rule 7(1) pertains to offences under the SC/ST Act and, therefore, they will be considered in different silos.

Mr. Mukesh Kalia, Counsel for the petitioner points out to a judgment of the Supreme Court in State of M.P. v. Chunnilal, (2009) 12 SCC 649, paras 8 and 9 of the said judgment are extracted hereunder:
"8.

entities.text: State of M.P. v. Chunnilal, (2009) 12 SCC 649
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The provisions in Section 9 of the Act, Rule 7 of the Rules and Section 4 of the Code when jointly read lead to an irresistible conclusion that the investigation of an offence under Section 3 of the Act by an officer not appointed in terms of Rule 7 is illegal and invalid.

But when the offence complained are both under IPC and any of the offence enumerated in Section 3 of the Act the investigation which is being made by a competent police officer in accordance with the provisions of the Code cannot be quashed for non-investigation of the offence under Section 3 of the Act by a competent police officer.

In such a situation the proceedings shall proceed in an appropriate court for the offences punishable under IPC notwithstanding investigation and the charge-sheet being not liable to be accepted only in respect of offence under Section 3 of the Act for taking cognizance of that offence.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 17/07/2024 at 01:11:39 9.
In the present case there is no denial of the fact that the accusations related to offences both under the Act and IPC.
The High Court was therefore not justified in quashing the entire proceedings.
The order shall be restricted to the offence under Section 3 of the Act and not in respect of offences punishable under IPC."

6. Accordingly, he contends that the determination by the Supreme Court is quite categorical in that the investigation of the IPC offences would continue whereas those under Section 3 of the SC/ST Act shall be quashed.

7. Second objection has been taken under Section 306 IPC which provides for punishment of a maximum of 10 years whereas Section 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST Act deals with offences with imprisonment for a term of 10 years or more.
8. The APP shall examine the petitioner's contentions on both these accounts and will present their submissions on the next date of hearing.

9. List on 31st July, 2024.
10.
Order be uploaded on the website of this Court.
ANISH DAYAL, J JULY 11, 2024/MK
